Prepared by Neal Austin Alfred  |  B.Com (Corporate Secretaryship), Loyola College Chennai  |  March 2026
1. CONSISTENT REVENUE GROWTH WITH FY24 MODERATION

TCS delivered a strong 17.6% revenue growth in FY2023, increasing from ₹1,91,754 crores to ₹2,25,458 crores. However, in FY2024, growth slowed to 6.8%, with revenue reaching ₹2,40,893 crores.This slowdown was largely driven by reduced IT spending from global clients, especially in the Banking, Financial Services & Insurance (BFSI) sector, as businesses navigated macroeconomic uncertainty and rising interest rates in the US and Europe.
Despite these headwinds, TCS still managed to maintain positive growth, highlighting the strength and resilience of its diversified client base.

Tata Consultancy Services consistently maintained a net profit margin of around 19% over the three-year period — a level widely regarded as best-in-class within the Indian IT industry. Its operating profit margin also stayed above 18%, reflecting strong cost discipline and operational efficiency. Despite employee benefit expenses being the largest cost component (around 55% of revenue), the company managed to keep this ratio stable even as its workforce expanded. This indicates that TCS has been able to effectively utilize its talent pool, driving productivity gains while scaling operations.
3. STRONG RETURN ON EQUITY REFLECTS CAPITAL EFFICIENCY

Tata Consultancy Services improved its ROE from 46.2% to 49.1%, meaning it earns about ₹0.49 profit for every ₹1 invested by shareholders. This is higher than most companies, showing strong efficiency, smart use of capital, and good management.
4. GROWING DIVIDEND SIGNALS STRONG CASH GENERATION

Tata Consultancy Services increased its dividend per share from ₹43 to ₹56 in three years (about 30% growth). It is also paying a slightly higher share of its profits to investors, backed by strong cash generation. This shows good financial health and a shareholder-friendly approach.

Tata Consultancy Services saw slower growth in FY2024, but its core business remains strong, supported by steady deal wins and expected demand from AI and cloud services. However, risks such as weak spending from banking clients, a stronger rupee impacting earnings, and employee attrition need to be monitored. Overall, TCS remains a stable, dividend-paying company with solid long-term growth potential.
⚠️  Disclaimer: This analysis is prepared for educational and portfolio demonstration purposes only. Data sourced from TCS Annual Reports and Screener.in.
